purpose: Add a "Speculation Rules URL Exclusion" textarea UI in Preload Settings to let users define custom URL patterns to exclude from speculation rules, with automatic WooCommerce cart/checkout/my-account page exclusion.
riskRationale: Well-contained feature following existing patterns with proper function_exists guards and WooCommerce detection. One edge case could break speculation entirely on plain-permalink sites, but the fix is trivial.

text: Clean implementation that follows the codebase's established patterns (textarea, Util::process_urls, conditional rendering, WooCommerce guards). Auto-detection of WooCommerce pages is a nice defensive touch. One important edge case (/* catch-all on plain permalink sites) must be fixed before merge. Minor issues around placeholder consistency and duplicate exclusion paths are worth addressing but not blocking.

reasoning: The /* catch-all on WooCommerce pages with plain permalinks silently breaks all speculation rules. The fix is a simple null/root-path guard.

message: WooCommerce auto-detection uses function_exists() guards and null-safe URL parsing, correctly handling the case when WooCommerce is not installed.
Exclude paths filter is registered unconditionally (regardless of speculation toggle), providing defense-in-depth for sensitive URLs even when speculation rules are managed by a third-party plugin.
Textarea uses aria-describedby to associate help text with the input, improving accessibility.
Good conditional-rendering test that verifies the exclude URLs field is hidden by default and appears only when speculation rules are enabled.
The updated "submits speculation settings" test correctly includes speculationExcludeUrls: '' in the expected payload, ensuring the default empty value is always sent.

When WooCommerce uses plain permalinks (e.g., example.com/?page_id=7), wp_parse_url($checkout_url, PHP_URL_PATH) returns /, and trailingslashit('/') . '*' produces /* — a catch-all pattern that inhibits all speculation rules. The same applies to the cart and my-account blocks below. While rare (WooCommerce strongly recommends pretty permalinks), this silently breaks speculation entirely.
suggestion: Add a guard to skip path extraction when $path is / (root path), since a root-level exclude of /* is almost certainly not the intent.

message: The textarea placeholder shows /checkout/* and /cart/* but omits /my-account/*, while the help text below mentions account pages are excluded automatically. This inconsistency could confuse users about expected URL formats. Additionally, showing these specific WooCommerce paths may mislead users into thinking they need to add them manually.
suggestion: Use a neutral placeholder like /my-plugin/*\n/excluded-path/* to avoid implying users should duplicate auto-detected paths, and add /my-account/* for consistency if keeping specific examples.

message: Uses get_permalink(wc_get_page_id('myaccount')) instead of the more idiomatic wc_get_page_permalink('myaccount'). Functionally equivalent but adds an unnecessary extra database lookup.
suggestion: Use wc_get_page_permalink('myaccount') for a single function call.

message: If a user manually enters /checkout/* (or /cart/*, /my-account/*) in the exclude URLs textarea, those paths will appear twice in the final exclude list — once from user input and once from WooCommerce auto-detection. Duplicates are harmless (browser dedupes) but bloat the JSON output.
suggestion: Filter out auto-detected paths that already exist in the user-provided list before appending WooCommerce paths, or add a deduplication pass at the end.
